repository.name: @webex/plugin-authorization-browser-first-party
repository.purpose: First-party (Webex web client) browser authorization plugin registered as webex.authorization. It starts OAuth authorization-code logins with CSRF state and PKCE (S256), completes them automatically on the redirect page load (CSRF check, URL scrubbing, best-effort preauth catalog, code exchange), supplies the browser token-refresh callback with public or confidential client authentication, handles the third-party login callback, runs device (QR code) login through the oauth-helper service with qRCodeLogin events, and redirects on logout.

public_interfaces.name: @webex/plugin-authorization-browser-first-party package entry
public_interfaces.audience: the webex package first-party entry (webex-first-party.js), recipe-private-web-client, and the Webex web client
public_interfaces.notes: Importing the package registers Authorization as public plugin 'authorization' with proxies isAuthorizing and isAuthenticating and the credentials config defaults. The first registration of the name wins, so import it before any other authorization plugin.

public_interfaces.name: webex.authorization runtime methods and events
public_interfaces.notes: initialize completes an authorization-code login automatically when the page URL has code. QR progress is reported only through qRCodeLogin events. eventEmitter is shared by all instances.

public_interfaces.name: credentials configuration defaults
public_interfaces.audience: integrators configuring Webex.init and webex-core credentials
public_interfaces.notes: clientType defaults to 'public' (client_id in the form); any other value uses HTTP Basic with client_secret for the code exchange and refresh. The device flow always uses HTTP Basic.

negative_guidance.rule: Do not rename or repurpose the sessionStorage keys oauth2-csrf-token and oauth2-code-verifier.
negative_guidance.why: A login started by one page load is completed by the next.

negative_guidance.rule: Do not send or log the raw email address.
negative_guidance.why: initiateLogin replaces it with its SHA-256 to reduce PII propagation.

negative_guidance.rule: Do not relax requireMatch on handleThirdPartyCallback.
negative_guidance.why: The third-party callback treats a missing stored CSRF token as a failure.

negative_guidance.rule: Do not treat README.md as the method, event, or error reference.
negative_guidance.why: Several README claims differ from code; see docs/adr/0001-retain-product-readme.md.

negative_guidance.rule: Do not run test:unit against a stale dist.
negative_guidance.why: The unit spec imports the package by name, which resolves main (dist/index.js).

negative_guidance.rule: Do not infer a coverage threshold for this package.
negative_guidance.why: The developer confirmed no coverage gate applies; the legacy Jest config disables coverage collection.

high.expectation: Source and unit test evidence both support the change, and the behavior has a case in test/unit/spec/authorization.js.

medium.expectation: Only source evidence exists, for example the 400 grant-error mapping, the missing-code rejection, registration, or the logout redirect. Pin current behavior with a characterization test before modifying.

low.expectation: Neither source nor tests settle the question. Stop and report the gap.
